 WSPA Spartanburg Spartanburg Water issues systemwide boil water advisory
 Nikolette Miller Wed, November 18, 2026 at 2:42 PM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. SPARTANBURG, S.C. (WSPA) – Spartanburg Water has issued a systemwide Boil Water Advisory for all customers served by its main water system after a significant loss of water pressure and/or service across the distribution network.
 The advisory applies to all customers in the main Spartanburg Water system, excluding Landrum customers.
 Officials said there has been no confirmed contamination of the water system. However, as a precaution, customers are being advised to boil all water used for drinking or cooking.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Spartanburg Water recommends bringing water to a boil for at least one full minute before using it for consumption. The utility also advises residents not to use ice made from water that was not boiled first.
 The advisory will remain in effect until further notice.
 Spartanburg Water said crews are working as quickly as possible to resolve the issue and restore normal service.
 Customers will be notified when the advisory has been lifted.
 Spartanburg Water serves nearly 240,000 people in Spartanburg County, as well as portions of Greenville, Union and Cherokee counties. The utility produces an average of 25 million gallons of drinking water daily and treats more than 14 million gallons of wastewater each day.
 Advertisement Advertisement Customers are encouraged to monitor Spartanburg Water for updates regarding the advisory.
